main_text.p: gentem non desinebat. Tum cōpulsi Iudæi vinctum eum Allophylis tradiderūt; sed traditus, ruptis vinculis arrepto {a}osse asini, quod calus telum dederat, mille ex hostibus prostravit. Ingravescente autem æstu, cum siti affectus esset, invocato Domino, {b}ex osse quod manu tenebat, aqua fluxit. Ea tempestate Samsō Hebræis præ-rat, Allophylis unius virtute domitis. Igi-tur inlidiantes vitę ejus, nec palam eum [?]ter-tare audentes, {c}uxore ejus, quam ille pe-stea[?] acceperat, pecunia corrumpūt, virtutem viri uti proderet. Illa eum blandimento mulicbri aggressa, diu eludentem & multum cūctatum perpulit, ut indicaret, in crinibus capitis virtutem suam subsistere. Mox dormienti insidiata, crinem ejus abstulit atq; ita eum Allophylis tradidit. Nam sæpe prius traditum coprehendere nequiverat. Tum illi effossis oculis vinctum compedibus in carcere conjecerunt. Sed spatio temporis accisus crinis crescere, & cū eis virtus redire occeperat. Iaq; Samson cōscius recepti roboris, tempus modo justæ ultionis {d}opperiebatur. Erat Allophylis moris, cum dies festos ageret, Samson quasi in pompam publicam producere,a maxillaex dente molari, qui erat in maxilla.DalilaIud. 16.oper. Col.Ibidem

page.notes: The side notes are printed in the right margin and are placed at the points where their marks stand in the text. The first note ("a maxilla") and the second note ("ex dente molari, qui erat in maxilla.") are marked a and b in the text. The "d" mark in the text is matched to "opper. Col." in the margin; the scan is faint there. The word "ter-tare" and the word "pe-stea" at the line ends are doubtful. A faint fragment in the bottom right corner (possibly show-through or a neighbouring page edge) is not transcribed. The word "calus" is copied as printed and may be a misprint for "casus".
